construct: Cyanide binds metal centers in mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase and halts oxidative phosphorylation, forcing anaerobic metabolism and causing severe lactic acidosis despite preserved oxygen delivery; failure of tissue oxygen extraction can produce unusually high venous oxygen saturation.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Cyanide exposure with severe lactic acidosis despite adequate arterial oxygenation and unusually oxygenated venous blood indicates histotoxic hypoxia from complex IV cytochrome c oxidase inhibition.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Complex I inhibition also arrests electron transport, but cyanide's canonical target is cytochrome c oxidase at complex IV; the exposure and physiology support that specific site.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: No other option explains both preserved oxygen delivery and failure of cellular oxygen utilization after cyanide exposure.
